definition: Knowledge-based recommender systems (knowledge based recommenders) are a specific type of recommender system that are based on explicit knowledge about the item assortment, user preferences, and recommendation criteria (i.e., which item should be recommended in which context).
details: These systems are applied in scenarios where alternative approaches such as collaborative filtering and content-based filtering cannot be applied. A major strength of knowledge-based recommender systems is the non-existence of cold start (ramp-up) problems. A corresponding drawback is a potential knowledge acquisition bottleneck triggered by the need to define recommendation knowledge in an explicit fashion.

explainer.lead: Knowledge-based recommender systems recommend items using explicit knowledge about the item assortment, user preferences and recommendation criteria. They matter in scenarios where collaborative filtering and content-based filtering cannot be applied.

tiers.eli5: Instead of guessing from what similar people liked, it follows written rules about what fits whom.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers encode which items should be recommended in which context so the recommender works without interaction history. The main pitfall is a knowledge acquisition bottleneck from having to define that recommendation knowledge explicitly.
tiers.paperLevel: They are based on explicit knowledge about the item assortment, user preferences and recommendation criteria. A major strength is the absence of cold start (ramp-up) problems; a drawback is a potential knowledge acquisition bottleneck.

explainer.example: A recommender without user history applies explicit criteria to match an item to a user's stated preferences.
